name: Bone-ash body
summary: A porcelain body that holds calcined bone ash, about 40 to 50 per cent, with china clay and china stone. It fires white and strong at a lower heat.
how: Burn animal bone to white ash and grind it fine.
Mix the ash with china clay and china stone.
Form the ware and fire the biscuit at about 1250 °C.
Glaze and fire again at a lower heat.

origin.note: Thomas Frye patents a porcelain with bone ash at the Bow works.

adoptions.via: Josiah Spode II fixes a bone china recipe that Staffordshire potters then use for tea and dinner services.
